chapter: Memphis, Oklahoma, the Kirk band and Kansas City
title: Recording with Blanche Calloway and the Brunswick date
summary: She sorts out the order of events: Blanche Calloway's Victor session came first, then the Pearl Theatre, then Brunswick refused to record Kirk unless she was there.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: When you worked at Pearl Theatre were you there with Andy Kirk's band or ...
With Andy Kirk's band.
But were you with Blanche Calloway?
I think that's when they had changed it to Blanche Calloway. Victor had recorded her like that also, Blanche Calloway and her band.
Were you in the band?
No, I was just still sitting there -
But it was Andy Kirk's band?
Yes, but they wouldn't record Jack; they recorded me. Decca told them to send for me from Kansas City, said they wouldn't record them if they didn't send for me.
WILLIAMS
It was Brunswick then. I received a wire. I was there, you know. They had left me in Kansas City.
Was this before the Pearl Theatre?
This was after the Pearl, I think.

Well, let's stick with the Pearl Theatre a minute. During the engagement at the Pearl Theatre it was Andy Kirk's band with you on piano, but actually it was called Blanche Calloway. And it was during that engagement that Blanche Calloway recorded for Victor? Were you in the same position?
Before we went into Pearl Blanche Calloway recorded for Victor, with the band, with her heading the bill.
'I Need Loving', was that one of the things you did?
Yes, that was that date.
Did you just do one session with Blanche?
I think so; we may have done two, for the tunes that you heard. We may have.
I see. Well, then, when did the Brunswick recording date come up?
That was later.
Was this the first recording you had ever done?
Yes, when I recorded with Blanche. That was before we went to the Pearl; I remember now because later on
